newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean investment abroad climbs sharply in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chilean investment abroad climbs sharply in 1996.

text.p: Chileans invested nearly $2 billion abroad in the first six months of the year with most spent in Argentina and Peru, although Brazil and Venezuela could soon prove just as attractive, said a report Thursday.

The study by Santiago's Chamber of Commerce painted a picture of Chilean businessmen rapidly moving abroad, with their investments climbing 23 percent on the first half of 1995 and set to remain buoyant as the drive to privatize state firms in Latin America gathers steam.
"The outlook for the medium term is encouraging," it said.
"The privatization process in Latin America will take on great dynamism in the second half of the year."
Around 150 state companies, including many in Brazil and Venezuela, are expected to be sold this year -- more than double the number privatized last year, said the report.
"In addition to Brazil, Venezuela represents a highly attractive destination for the internationalization of Chilean firms in coming years," said the chamber.

A large number of sales will be in the electricity sector, where Chilean power companies have a considerable advantage, it said. Some Chilean companies already control some utilities in Argentina and Peru.
Chile, Latin America's most successful economy, is one of the top investors in the region, with figures from the chamber showing investments totalling around $10 billion since 1990.
Argentina has received most of Chilean foreign investment so far this year, with $1.3 billion spent mainly in projects in energy and industrial sectors.
Investment in Peru totalled $360 million with most projects in the electricity sector.

Against the trend was Bolivia, where investment plunged an "alarming" 43 percent on the same period last year, possibly as the result of a wave of anti-Chilean protests in the country, said the report.

Both countries, which have long had thorny relations over border disputes dating from the last century, will have to give positive signals of stability before Chilean companies are prepared to resume investing in Bolivia, said the chamber.
Investment in privatizations, which has driven Chilean firms' expansion abroad this decade, totalled just $79 million with Chileans buying four state companies.

The chamber said its data is based on projects reported through formal and informal sources, with investments which are spread over more than a year included in the year which they are first announced.
Central Bank figures, based on materialised investments, are more conservative and show Chilean firms have invested $3.2 billion abroad since 1975.
